purpose: Text that ships in this public repository's history must not carry operator-environment detail. Commit messages and annotated tag messages are permanent and world-readable once pushed.
scope_note: These rules cover GENERIC classes only. They deliberately do not encode any organisation-specific hostname, account name or internal identifier prefix, because a denylist of internal identifiers committed to a public repository publishes the shape of those identifiers to everyone who reads it. Checks for those belong in private tooling. This file's own contents are safe to publish, and that is a design constraint rather than an accident.

documentation_addresses.why: Reserved ranges that exist to be written down. Carved out ONCE, centrally, so that no two rules can reach opposite verdicts on the same address. This repository legitimately uses them in its own examples.

trailer_exemption.why: A mandated Co-Authored-By trailer carries an address, which would otherwise trip the host rule on nearly every commit. The exemption is deliberately narrow: only the ADDRESS PORTION of a well-formed trailer, only in the FINAL paragraph. An earlier implementation blanked the whole line for any key matching cc/author/committer anywhere in the message, which made `Author: <anything>` lint clean - and `Author:` is the first token you get when pasting git log output into a message.

rules.why: The session trailer belongs only on private repositories. It links a public commit to an internal transcript. (Matched with horizontal whitespace only: a `\s*` here consumes the preceding newline and reports the wrong line.)
A session URL is a direct pointer into private conversation history.
A bare session identifier is the same disclosure as the URL without the scheme.
RFC 1918 and RFC 6598 addresses describe someone's internal network topology.
An absolute home path names a local account and the layout of a machine that is not this repository.

A personal checkout path describes a working environment rather than the code; refer to paths relative to the repository root. Dotfile-rooted paths such as ~/.local or ~/.config are deliberately NOT matched: they are standard locations that name neither a user nor a machine, and an earlier revision of this rule produced a false positive on ~/.local/bin in a real tag message.
A worktree name is local scaffolding and means nothing to a reader of this repository.

A login paired with an address is a credential-shaped hint about a specific machine. Bounded to IP literals on purpose: a bare hostname cannot be distinguished from an ordinary email domain without naming the organisation's hosts, which this file must not do.
A MAC address identifies one physical interface and is stable for the life of the hardware.
IPv6 unique-local and link-local addresses describe an internal network. A link-local address derived from a MAC also outlives the interface it names.

finding_precedence.why: A session trailer line also matches the URL and bare-id rules, so an unsuppressed scan reports three findings for one problem. Three findings for one problem trains a reader to skim, which is how a fourth, real finding gets missed.
